summary: This work develops a co-designed architecture combining Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC) and Quantum Error Detection (QED) on logical qubits, deriving conditions for sampling advantage and introducing steady-state extraction to handle position-dependent error behavior in QED codes. On a $[[6,4,2]]$ Iceberg code running QAOA at depths $p=4$--$8$, PEC+QED achieves $2$--$11\times$ lower absolute error and up to $31\times$ lower MSE versus PEC on physical qubits.
motivation: QED reduces noise efficiently at low qubit overhead but leaves residual bias; PEC can correct this residual error in software but has exponential cost in noise strength. If QED reduces per-gate noise below a threshold, PEC's sampling savings can outweigh QED's discard overhead, but realizing this requires addressing two system-level design challenges around QED interval placement and error characterization.
method: The work derives an efficiency condition $\epsilon_p - \epsilon_\ell / p_\mathrm{rej} > 1/4$ for sampling advantage (Equation 1) and shows the canonical minimum interval $L=1$ does not achieve break-even in any evaluated code, while optimized intervals on high-rate Iceberg codes do. To handle position-dependent error dynamics from the first QED cycle's transient leakage injection, the authors develop steady-state extraction: a characterization protocol that inverts out the first-cycle transient via superoperator inversion ($S_\mathcal{G} = S_\mathcal{G}^\mathrm{concat} \circ S_\mathrm{init}^{-1}$), isolating the steady-state channel that governs subsequent gates.
result: Steady-state extraction reduces observable bias by up to $10.2\times$ below QED-only baselines across depolarizing, amplitude damping, and dephasing noise (Figure 6). At $10^5$ attempted shots on $[[6,4,2]]$ Iceberg code QAOA, PEC+QED achieves absolute error of $6.0 \times 10^{-4}$ (p=4), $1.7 \times 10^{-3}$ (p=6), $9.0 \times 10^{-5}$ (p=8) versus QED-only at $2.9 \times 10^{-3}$, $3.0 \times 10^{-3}$, $2.6 \times 10^{-3}$; quasi-probability norm $\gamma$ stays below $1.01$ for PEC+QED versus $1.053$--$1.108$ for PEC-only, with acceptance rates $90$--$94\%$.
